reviews.text: An early review, but very fun so far. There is a very clear metaprogression here, based around using characters as leaders or accomplishing certain goals with characters during each run. Characters only have two equipment slots for active and passive skills to start, but you can find items each run to increase these slots. Each equipment piece can change the way a character plays or give new tactics (pushing enemies, lunging towards enemies, attacking from behind). The positioning system, the enemy skill forecast, and the split between movement points and action points all combine to create a very fast but tactical combat system that I'm looking forward to digging into.

The game is alright, but definitely needs some work before I can consider investing more time into it. You definitely need a 4th party member by the time you reach the second map since there's a HUGE jump in difficulty between maps 1 and 2. Also, the co-op system could use some adjustments as well. Your party members don't always attack with you, for some reason, and it leaves you scratching your head since you expect them to combo with you, then the enemy survives with like 1-2 HP and he gets a free turn. If you're standing next to a party member or in the same tile as them, it should guarantee a co-op attack every single time, plain and simple. In its current state, it feels very mobile-like, just from the vibe I'm getting anyway, and early access. It ALMOST feels like a complete game, but they just need to tweak some things here and there to get it right. Kinda regretting not checking out the demo beforehand since I had it downloaded, but just never had the chance to play it. I decided to pick this up tonight and it's just too unbalanced right now, imo. Also, you basically HAVE to die to get better skills, stats, etc. which is kinda lame, since it punishes you for doing everything right, but you aren't supposed to clear the content yet because you're not "strong" enough. So yeah, that kinda sucks too. Not exactly my first time playing a game with roguelike qualities, but it is certainly my first time playing one that punishes you for playing properly and just gatekeeps you out of content with a stat difference you can't overcome unless you die. I don't really care much for games that force losses on you with artificial difficulty like that, forcing you to go back through the same area for an hour or two and HOPE that RNG is actually in your favor with the random loot. Anyway, in its current state, I can't really recommend the game, but I can see how some might find it enjoyable if they're not familiar with games that do what this one does, but better.

早在2012年，荒木飞吕彦老师便借由子安武人(《JOJO的奇妙冒险》贯穿始终的大反派迪奥的CV)之口，告诉我们：人的力量，终究是有限度的。 在整整12年之后，又一个游戏制作组RocketPunch Games再次贯彻了迪奥老师的理念，让《异界失控》的硬核机甲画风一转福瑞风： 我们可以看初版和试玩封面图(正式版不太像了所以还是用试玩版)的对比，会发现甚至几位角色POSE都没变，就纯纯的是把角色变成了福瑞。让我不禁感叹：制作组naive，以为福瑞主角就能让玩家屈服了么？然后我发现是的——好家伙换了画风关注度暴涨是吧？ 这款游戏在之前的试玩版就展示出来十分出色的游戏素质，可以认为是我玩过的最好的类《暗黑地牢》游戏(纯可玩性而言大胜多娜多娜)，其实暗黑地牢并不易模仿(因为它本质上其实是一个数值游戏)，就连Red Hook Studios自己的续作也因为改成肉鸽模式(和在EPIC独占了1年)惨遭多半好评。 多年后我们能发现最好的暗黑地牢代餐，大概是打了美少女MOD的“少女地牢”，而真正的“少女地牢”比如《圣铠冰魂》玩法质量惨不忍睹，不过《异界失控》的出现是第一次让我眼前一亮：原来《暗黑地牢》的继承者，除了“少女地牢”之外，还有福瑞地牢，那么它是如何做到的呢？ [h1]提前预警的回合制玩法[/h1] 《暗黑地牢》类游戏难以复制的原因，除了上文提到的数值设计，最大的难点在于“回合制中的可控性”——《暗黑地牢》把这个玩法简化为1、2、3、4号位的站位规则，从此以外的要素其实只包含命中率和暴击带来的意外、以及血量和san值的平衡，但糅合出了简约而不简单的玩法内容。 [h2]还是“一字长蛇阵”，但加上时间要素[/h2] 那么后续的作品往往需要做加法，比如蓝洞有一款类似游戏是把站位扩成了3×4的队列——类似做法的还有《为了吾王》，但是这些游戏都没有给玩家足够的可控性。 那么《异界失控》是怎么做的呢？还是利用位置，但是加入了“生效时间”：敌人的攻击会先给一个回合的反应时间——攻击面前的、攻击面前一段区域的、周身AOE的等诸多类型，那么就给了我们足够的反应时间来规避这次伤害。 以下图为例，敌人和我方的血量差距巨大，不过基本敌人的攻击是有“弹道”而非“锁头”，给了操作的可能性——我们的特工狐狸可以移动到它身后，兔子医师则可以后撤一步，就能避开攻击。在《异界失控》中，不存在传统xcom式游戏的“攻击后结束回合”设定，所以可以达成非常自己的操作顺序，这一方面增加了容错率；另一方面和共容易达成和队友的配对合击。 [h2]冲锋、闪烁与击退[/h2] 由于敌人的攻击延时，所以附带位移的技能可以很轻松的创造优势，比如冲锋可以让我们更快的接近后排的危险敌人、闪烁可以切入战场或者从包围中逃离，击退则可以大幅改变敌人的位置让他们聚集——这里共同用到的是，是位置的概念，与《暗黑地牢》到《多娜多娜一起做坏事》不同，在《异界失控》中每个格子存在3格空间，你可以进入队友或者对手所在的格子里。 那么“每个格子存在3格空间”，就带来了本作在增加玩家“可控性”方面做的第二个文章，那就是： [h1]被颠覆的站位规则——横轴的扩展性[/h1] 长久以来，我见过的所有类《暗黑地牢》游戏，基本是一个格子一个坑，那么这种你可以进入其他角色所处的格子的设定，是我见过的最为有意思的设计了。 且它和上一段提到的“攻击的延迟生效”产生了十分有趣的化学反应，比如敌人朝面前的攻击你可以绕到背后，“旋风斩”类型的攻击你可以和它站在同一格。 此外游戏包含很多牵引和击退类型的技能&物品设计，都可以创造出围绕“位置”的变化。 [h2]墙角、拥挤和超拥挤[/h2] 和敌人的特殊位置能产生效果——当同一个格子容纳两个单位时会进入“拥挤”，容纳三个单位时进入“超拥挤”状态——超拥挤状态下其他角色无法用“冲刺”技能以外的方式通过，且回合结束时格子内单位会受到伤害。 关于“超拥挤”状态，需要注意的是部分BOSS本身就具有很大的体型，此外熊的盾击之类的技能也可以主动制造敌人“超拥挤”的不利局面——此外由于被逼入墙角的单位会增到额外伤害，如果熊在墙角壁咚敌人，产生的撞击效果也十分惊人！ [h2]合击、夹击与专业辅助的登场[/h2] 当你和队友包围敌人时可以触发夹击，此外如果你和队友站在同一格内，当你攻击时就会触发队友的追击——哪怕是兔子医师的2格射击也会触发狐狸和狗熊的射击追加，所以，让我不禁想问：你两的枪平时为什么不能用？只有泡妞时才能发动是吧？(bushi) 和队友合击的效果，受到“支援”数值的影响，此外部分被动异常物也可以大幅增强其效果，比如你给兔子医师安装一个“+1支援距离”的被动异常物，就会让她的使用灵活很多。 支援在游戏中，因为有很多联动的“异常物”，可以产生十分夸张的效果，比如兔妹的支援可以触发给队友回血、加甲、加瞄准BUFF(所有属性+1)、甚至可以给自己15%几率回行动力......因为支援的效果过去逆天，游戏中我甚至不能触发支援的攻击都不想A出去。 [h2]1.0版本：丰富到不可思议的改变[/h2] 我受邀提前试玩了1.0版本的游戏，总的来说，本文远远不足以展现1.0版本带来的改变： 比如完整的4章章节、困难模式隐含的真结局、完成的角色解锁内容、职业专属技能被改为主动物品且可在休息屋养成——其实我不太喜欢这个改动，因为让原本就紧张的主动异常物栏位雪上加霜。 但尽管不是福瑞控，我已经迫不及待的想要分享这款游戏，因为这和《孤星猎人》一起，一并成为了在“战斗的可操控感”上最能满足我的游戏，如果你对《暗黑地牢》风格的游戏有兴趣，那么这款游戏绝对不容错过！ ++提前预警+站位规则带来的无限战斗可能性 +可爱的福瑞画风(我不是福瑞控但确实挺可爱的) +局内构筑的多样可能性 +局外丰富的角色构筑 -组队的自由程度：随机队伍缺奶妈或者缺远程都会比较难打 -UI丑
非常好游戏, 如果没有东风、西风、死了原地僵挺一回合、重力黑洞就更好了.

Great game to play on steam deck. It runs fantastic, considering the day 1 release the minor hiccups I had with the controller layout not registering properly is honestly not that bad. On to teh game proper, it's a tactical game ala into the breach where positioning and manipulating positioning is king You get COMBO attacks when you're on the same tile as another friendly, or you can get flank bonus by ping ponging enemies into friendlies. There's also minimal RNG so the feedback of building a good team or conversely a bad team is immediate in the next fight.
异界失控又称猫羊栓条狗（格利奇：？）都能过，协作攻击套路比其他套路强的不是一点半点，协同乘区比暴击更高效而且更加稳定，甚至无法保障攻击频率猫羊互相协作也有很高的强度了。至于远方的蓄力体系。。。要是不能救还是埋了吧（刚需那个动后休息的遗物，建议改成上回合不攻击，不然原地睡觉在后期基本是瞬间蒸发）
期待了好久，上架就买了。build系统做的也好，有风、黑洞和倾斜等场地效果。普通难度很简单，对经常玩肉鸽和战旗的玩家来说很容易。就是有局外成长导致前几局基本都是堆成长了。第三把给狗哥刷出build，直接拿下普通难度。冲着小羊打了一下午，命是连击的狗哥给的，命是给小羊的。

玩法还不错，在回合制战斗这个做烂了的题材里做出了自己的一套玩法。 但是价格相对于当前内容量，即使是有了捆绑包折扣的8折也是偏高。 部分随机因素过于搞心态（诸如西风东风晶壳死而不僵......）负反馈远大于正反馈，建议删掉！ 狂暴阶段＋无限生怪是哪个天（n）才（t）设计的？搭配奇奇怪怪搞人心态的随机因素，直接把原本就剩几下解决的战斗变成又臭又长的拉锯战甚至直接翻车，一场战斗拖到后期还没解决难道不是你游的机制问题？ 局外成长要素太多，作为一款肉鸽却过于强调局外成长，导致前期玩的几把注定是折磨，不合理！ 战利品选择界面强烈建议增加浏览角色属性与背包的功能,不理解前辈们摸索出来的优秀经验为什么不直接学习!

Anomaly Collapse happened to be one of those games that just [i]clicked[/i] with me, and, despite the issues I found with it, it's really hard for me to put the game down. At its surface, AC is your usual turn-based roguelike RPG, and honestly, that's pretty much all it is. There's some semblance of a story, but it's pretty bare-bones and the writing feels kind of robotic, often leaving the impression that the characters are forced to explain game mechanics in a way that makes sense within the game's universe. The art style is alright -- I like the character designs, but the a lot of enemy designs look kind of flat and unmemorable; the environments have this "made on a budget" feeling to them that's kind of hard to put into words. That being said, what really hooked me are the game mechanics. Like most of my favorite games, the core concepts are very simple: [list] [*]You get 1 action and 2 movement per turn [*]Actions can be shared with other party members [*]Skipping a turn entirely gets you an extra action [*]Different player and enemy abilities have different minimum and maximum attack ranges [/list] But very quickly the game layers a lot of different conditional mechanics on top of that: [list] [*]You can flank and corner enemies [*]Attacking with an ally on your tile makes them attack with you [*]Some abilities can push enemies, which is extra effective when pushing them into corners or each other [*]As you play, combats begin having modifiers, such as "at the end of the round, the left-most unit is pushed to the right" and "a meteorite lands on a designated tile each round, blocking movement" [*]Each character's abilities can be customized with passive and active abilities that you find [/list] All of this combined creates an experience where each turn is a puzzle where you're trying to manipulate the enemy positioning and targeting in the most advantageous way possible while trying to finish the encounter in a reasonable amount of time before the anti-stalling mechanics trigger. I found this puzzle-solving to be very satisfying, and the game seems to encourage that, lacking damage ranges on most damaging skills and giving the player a limited in-game "undo turn" resource that you can use in case you realized a mistake or forgot some interaction. With that in mind, there are some issues that make the experience more tedious than it needs to be. Almost all status effects lack unique icons, using an up and down arrows for buffs and debuffs respectively; there is no combat log that you can read through to see what [i]exactly[/i] happened on any given turn (you are notified when some abilities trigger, but it's only the name of the ability, and it goes away quickly); the game is somewhat lacking in action previews -- you can see the damage you are going to do, whether or not you're flanking and your crit chance -- but there are no previews for DOTs or for the damage of supporting attacks. I also think that some actions, like movement, should have undo options that aren't resource-limited. Lastly, the game features an extensive meta-progression screen for each character, where you're encouraged to complete certain tasks for significant increase in power. As an example, on your first run you only get 4 equipment slots per character. You can get that number up to 9, a 125% increase, by leveling up. I'm personally not a fan of meta progression in roguelikes where you get more powerful, but in this game it's pretty fast, and completing your first run isn't [i]impossible[/i], though I only did it by cheating and resetting 3 combats. I do wish you could look up the quests your characters need to do to level up though, as some of them are quite specific. Overall, while I really enjoy this game, I think there are a lot of improvements that could be made, especially in the UX department, that leave me feeling like the game should have been released in Early Access for a couple of months. If you are able to look past these issues like I have, then this is a really fun experience that has a lot of content and replay value.

It's a pity but I have to refund this. Let's start with the good stuff: 1)The mechanics are interesting and I find the stacking character mechanic on the same tile to be innovative. 2)The soundtrack is pretty good 3)The setting and character designs are really good as well. 4)Being able to save and stop between fights in the same run was a blessing to have. Not all roguelikes/lite have this feature. Now to the drawbacks that made me not recommend the game. 1)I knew this was a roguelite from the start but the game seemed to have a plot going on but I couldn't stop myself from comparing it to Hades, which is another roguelike that managed to add a lot of character development and story. Honestly, either remove all story and have the game be focused solely on combat (akin to games like vampire survivor and forager) or actually give depth to the world and characters. There was next to no character banther out side of the recruitiing and maybe a boss and even that was shallow. It feels like a disappointment because the deisgns and setting were so good but the game failed to hook me with the storytelling. 2)the metaprogression is quite bad. You can slowly unlock some perks for a character but it feels like there was next to no actual progress between runs. It doesn't feel like I made any progress when I start a new run. 3)The unlockable characters are the only thing that could spice things up in team composition but they end up being unlocked waay too late into the game to be interesting or rewarding especially if someone, like me, can't get past halfway of the second map. So, i'm stuck with the first three characters and have to use the same skills over and over again. This also circles back to my complaint about the story. The tutorial hooked me with the setting and interaction between Glitch and Mira. Then, when I finished the tutorial, I'm suddenly rewarded with Stray without any ceremony or cutscene only so I could have a 3 person team from the start. Maybe I can unlock one or two more if I get past the halfway point of map 2 but it just doesn't feel interesting anymore to use the same characters over and over again, especially when I don't find their skillset very engaging. The game doesn't give me reason to keep on trying. I know that the team working on this is small. Maybe I'm too harsh on the game but the more promise a game shows, the disappointment feels bigger when it doesn't deliver.
Some nice ideas but further refinements needed, not least of all the interface and overworld gameplay. To revisit in future.

[h1] 《异界失控》简评 [/h1] [h1] 前言 [/h1] 本作是由RocketPunch Games制作，Spiral Up Games发行的一款以福瑞为主角的可以走位的肉鸽回合制策略游戏。 [h1] 美术 [/h1] 本作的美术方面绝对是本作的一大亮点，游戏新颖地采用了以福瑞风格配合游戏的动画渲染效果，整体画面表现精致，各个人物的服装表现都有其特色，同时人物周围添加了一层描边设计，使得人物更加立体生动，而加上游戏的动画渲染效果在线，人物的各种动作流畅，整体视觉效果非常不错。 [h1] 剧情 [/h1] 游戏的剧情比较碎片化，需要玩家一步步推进关卡来解锁，游戏的背景设定比较新颖，在这个世界中有各种异常事件的出现，而相对应的为了解决这些事件的发生，诞生了异常应对管理局，在一次事件中一个强大的怪物出现，导致小队卷入了另一个世界，主角团们也失忆了，而玩家将在这个异界进行探索，找到事件的真相。 [h1] 玩法 [/h1] 游戏的玩法依旧是上手容易精通难的特点，玩家需要根据怪物的攻击来进行走位躲避，在安全的位置释放技能和攻击进行反击，每个人物都有两点移动力和一点行动力，行动力可以保留。 听起来玩法还是比较简单的，但游戏加入了三人小队玩法，开始选择的一名角色可以作为领队，拥有领队效果，而在关卡推进途中则会遇到其他队员，最多三名，每个队员都有其不同的技能和特性。 因为屏幕上怪物和队友人数都比较多，游戏很有趣的引入了拥挤机制，每个格子最多只能站三个人，一旦超过就会过度拥挤从而扣血。而三人站在一起时一位队友攻击敌人就会触发协同攻击，额外造成伤害，同时也可以两人形成包夹，夹击有额外的攻击加成等等，可以说人数的增多以及战斗系统的新颖系统使得游戏的策略玩法提高了不少，玩家可以思考出不同的解法解决敌人。 游戏目前有四个章节，八个角色，超过200多种的主动和被动道具，需要注意的是，角色和道具都会随着玩家完成的条件逐步解锁，也就是说你玩的越久，解锁的道具和角色就越多，游戏的可玩性也越来越高，也就是本作的局外成长方面并不需要资源的获取，而是更加鼓励玩家多次游玩进行挑战， [h1] 总结 [/h1] 整体美术、玩法质量都很在线的回合制肉鸽策略游戏，游戏画面精致，肉鸽要素齐全，可玩性很高，值得一试。 [quote] 执笔勾墨色，挥毫著文章；阳春布德泽，璞玉生光辉 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44174077/]吟遊诗人的手札[/url]，书游戏特色，写游戏魅力 [/quote]

Its good don't get me wrong but it's also bad. The reason is that it feels very limiting and it makes it difficult. EDIT: 1 year has passed since I played this game last. Its still just as hard, just as confusing, and just as needlessly complicated. Whatever balance changes, tune-ups, or patches that have been added are not in any way visible in the opening stages of the game. I am getting crushed every single game, what a waste of money! =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= A furry rogue-like that, after a few tutorials, throws you into the absolute deep-end of an utterly-overwhelming battle system. -Sometimes enemies can travel through your squares, even if you can't this yourself. -Sometimes being in the same square as your allies HURTS you. -Sometimes one of your party members becomes a living time bomb for no descernable reason. -Sometimes you start battles with massive de-buffs for no descernable reason. -Sometimes stronger foes will just SUMMON even more powerful foes for no descernable reason, garunteeing a loss to snatch you from the jaws of victory. -Sometimes there will be little drones on the ground and if you activate them yourself, they will instantly become hostile and give buffs to the monsters and not to you. -Sometimes stacking allies into the same space makes it "crowded", which means you are more likely to get critically hit, even if the game encourages you to stack up for co-op attacks. -Sometimes the main character has a gun, most of the time he doesn't. It only seems to appear during co-op attacks, but isn't available otherwise. -A STAGGERING number of enemies come with the ability "Last Breath", which means if you kill them, you don't kill them. They get up again with a chunk of health for one more turn so they can hit you just one more time before dropping dead. Which of course makes combats with them even harder than it already is. -ALL of the map/campaign/battle effects that get added are bad. Lightning storms. Extra Spores. Wierd Gravity. Burning Panels. There is not a single effect that I have seen that does anything other than make the run harder or more tedious. We can't have ONE good effect so we feel like its our lucky day? All of it has to be bad or hurt you? All of these complaints happened to me within the first HOUR of gameplay. Unfortunately the game also runs on the rogue-like philosophy that you MUST lose. You must lose many, many, many times until the RNG gods favor you with a good start or the proper unlock to begin the game with a good fighting chance. I don't enjoy games that do this. I would rather win. Win on my own merit based on skill, not on random circumstance or how many times I've beaten my head against a wall for the proper unlock. Losing 20 times to be able to start the game with a good piece of gear, THEN winning is not my cup of tea. I won't ask for a refund, a lot of love and care clearly went into this and the makers deserve credit, but I will not be recommending it to anyone either. There is too much here to not like or to wonder why it was necessary.

局外天赋树让这个游戏黯然失色。 如果这个成长放到游戏本体里，随着人物升级给出，然后局外成长是加强一部分机制的数值或者内容，那我感觉就无敌了。 比如开局不应该只有一个技能，2-3个技能的开局才让安全屋的拿主动事件更有意义。 比如被动完全就可以开局给出若干个，而不是选个新人物发现我没解锁的情况下，升级只有最简单的数值收益。 比如局外成长可以增加开局技能的强度上限（在打完第一层/二层等加强技能） …… 可惜了现在是一坨。在人物没有解锁局外成长的时候升级都没有什么感觉。 第一把剧情杀，第二把惨死，第三把死四图60%解锁，第四把60%的功能全解锁+过普通结局。第五把开始90%解锁的小羊就已经可以带着2个纯粹的休息工具人爆杀标准难度，这是0解锁的角色完完全全做不到的。 但是换个角色又得从头体验解锁的傻逼。只能说幸好小羊的强度体现在协同攻击上，可以一直让想解锁的人物拿人头，从而快速解锁。所以我真的是在玩肉鸽lite游戏吗，我宁愿觉得它是重复刷刷刷游戏。

Another game with such good artwork and game-play premise held back by abysmal game design and balance. The turn based elements and grid based positioning system are a classic format that is implemented well here, and the gameplay loop is fun in that regard. The deep rooted problem with this game is the balancing is nothing short of atrocious, all encounters after the 1st area have 5+ enemies (vs only your party of 3, if that) with way too much health and significantly better move sets than anything the party can get their hands on. Enemies and bosses also tend to have a constant stream of reinforcements and modifiers consisting anywhere from dealing extra damage to fully resurrecting/enduring killing blows. The meta progression doesn't even begin to fill in the power gap between enemies and players, your progress rewards are lackluster and no matter how many stat boosts or items you get, you always feel weak. Even the forced common encounters the game gives you the illusion of "picking" even have 5+ mobs that can completely wipe your team just from sheer numbers and AP cucking. There's alot more that could be said about this game, however this review is already long and rambling. This game has the potential to succeed and succeed well, which is why I feel so frustrated with it's current state, I wholeheartedly hope things can be turned around in the future. Tldr quick points: Pros: fun gameplay loop, good character artwork Cons: game balance is bad (enemies, area modifiers, player strength etc.), meta-progression is unrewarding, story/writing is bland, illusion of choice route picking with no real rewards worth the punishment. Refund denied, I hope this game can change for the better, but for now, i'll be dropping it and cannot recommend at this time. *edited to add additional points and tone down frustrations.

不推荐，看后续游戏的更新会调整评价。目前来看，画风是这款游戏最吸引人的地方，但是玩下来总体感觉，这款游戏的核心机制有点问题。 第一个是过载和行动点机制，你不得不去存行动点去打输出（不然就是每个人A一下，不痛不痒，你跟我说角色技能联动？不存在的，除非制作组理解的联动是给关键角色挂BUFF），这就基本上决定了三个角色，其中有两个是打辅助，一个打输出，这就固定了游戏通关的玩法，而且我想玩单角色话，这几乎是不可能的，毕竟没有其他两个角色给行动点了。 第二个是选人的机制，真别抽奖了，就让玩家一开始把角色选好（起码有个羊压力会小很多），而且抽奖会让玩家想玩的套路很难成型，或许制作组也觉得反正角色之间没技能联动，就随意了。 第三个是游戏难度问题，起码我觉得DUBUFF章节不用随机，你就公开了，让玩家自己选嘛，有时候随机到恶心的章节真的无语，特别是角色还没成型的时候，那就直接GG。还有来点BUFF章节，玩家也玩得爽嘛。

This is one of those recommendations where I wish there was a "sorta" option instead of yes/no - I all-but flipped a coin to decide if I'd put this one down as positive or negative. However the question it asks isn't "did you have some fun" or "did you feel you got your money's worth?" but exactly "would you RECOMMEND it?" I do so with a huge amount of caveats. The game has a heavy metaprogression element, so unless you're an expert at the genre like I am you'll probably lose your first few runs just because your characters are hugely underpowered. On the flip side, the metaprogression powerrs up characters in a rather linear way - this isn't one of those games with tons of builds and options to explore. On the first runs it'll LOOK like that, but that's because you didn't unlock everyone's passives yet. Once you have, you realize that everyone pretty much has 1 "real" build that works with all of their kit - doing anything else just turns them into a far-inferior version of another character. Stray is your knockback character, Glitch snowballs off killing sprees, Anomy rests and then spams ranged attacks, Mira heals a bit and does insane damage via coop support, yada yada. Despite there being a lot of cool items, fairly few of them actually fundamentally change how you play. And when you get them, they're a ton of fun! But they're the exception, and after a few runs you'll quickly realize that every time you get access to one of the game's merely 8 characters they play basically identically. That said, the identical play in question involves pretty fun mechanics. The emphasis on positioning and knockback is great. The "factors" mechanic, again, involves introduces modifiers that seem pretty fun at first and mix up how you play, and only really falter after you've played 3-4 runs and realize you're seeing all the same identical stuff over and over and over. I wouldn't necessarily complain here, but this is a roguelike that profoundly lacks any variety, while still missing any of the advantages of being a non-roguelike (like interesting choices, tight pacing, actual compelling writing/setting, etc). For what it's worth, I also found the game very easy - the only challenging runs I had were my first 2, because I had to beat them with zero meta-progression when all of your characters are literally missing like 25% of their stats, 60% of their slots and 80% of their passives, and many of them are missing their strongest options for starting skills as well, and without having other options for starting skills the "pick a starting skill you didn't start with" option at camp is useless, further nerfing your characters. But under those conditions, I found it pretty challenging and had to adapt to what I found since my characters weren't already OP right out of the box. Ever since I unlocked more stuff, runs have stopped being half as compelling. My first run on the so-called "harder" difficulty was an absolute breeze and I can't even tell you what's supposed to be harder. The only thing I noticed was that the final boss had 600 hp instead of 400 hp - I didn't notice any other differences as I killed most fights on turn 1 or 2 in a repetitive way 30+ times in a row. That said, I am an expert at the genre and it's very likely you won't have that same issue quite as quickly - from what I can tell most people don't win their first upgrade-less run by far. And when the game is challenging, it's never from how the bosses are designed or anything - it's more just because a bunch of random modifiers get stacked up on a normal fight to where it gets hard to keep track of all the random wind pushing things around, black holes sucking them up, debuffs randomly moving your guys around when you kill enemies, etc. Which can be interesting, but you're still more often screwed over by forgetting one than because you ended up in an unwinnable position due to an actual mistake with a decision. I still think it can be fun, and if you're the sort of casual person who's just happy to try a few times until the buffs on characters add up to a victory, maybe see 1 or 2 cool builds and then call it a day, you probably will enjoy the game. You're just also not the sort of person in my circle of friends that I might give this game a recommendation to. Otherwise, the fact that this game has a pretty poor amount of content and gets repetitive very quickly, means it fails to be something I would actually recommend to players that want a tactical roguelike. Unlike most roguelikes, this game gets less and less fun with every run, so if you're hoping for a game that'll be fun for more than 10ish hours, this isn't the place for your money. Though if that sounds good to you, go for it - the core combat loop is pretty solid and at least seeing every character once can be a bit interesting, although it can feel a bit hollow since you know you aren't making your own cool build by noticing the right stuff, but just following the choo-choo tracks the developers set for you. (P.S. Also, the game's damage projections suck - they don't tell you how much damage your ally's support will do or what your crit damage would be or such, so it means unless you memorize a bunch of numbers you won't know if your attack will kill an enemy. In a game where knowing if you can kill someone is vital to a ton of abilities, that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I might legit tell you not to play this game for that reason alone - this WILL frustrate you.)

While i wish i could leave a positive review, i feel like most people who are interested in this game are going to be tricked by its appearance and the way the game presents itself to start, but once you hit the gameplay loop it becomes a pretty unforgiving slog of progression, every run feels like youre just making a few steps towards a greater goal, without any real motivation to keep pulling you forward, It becomes very repetitive fast and youre forced to go through the same scenarios with the same characters to try to push their progression far enough to where they become powerful, but by that time youre bored of using them or they become unenjoyable to use because they fall into a singular playstyle. The game starts as unforgiving and interesting but quickly loses its edge as the progression contradicts the difficulty, which mostly spawns from the action economy and "death spiral" like random mechanics that turn what should be a strategic game into a total coin flip of "end of turn" effects which all usually stack up into you losing your characters unexpectedly which is one of the most frustrating ways to lose a run. I want to give this game the benefit of having Devs who are keeping an eye on the comments and patching the game still, but ending every session on a frustrating loss and closing the game not feeling like i want to play it again isnt a very positive experience or one that lends itself into easily recommending this game to others.

This game DEMANDS that you rush and have enough damage in order to complete it. The entire game itself is pretty much Darkest Dungeon's Farmstead from the Color of madness dlc where you will fight wave after wave of enemies with the map having some way to mess with your party but it has an ending. You do not have to complete the entire run in one sitting, you can save and come back later. In between these fights you will get events which are kinda a break away from combat, but can also be another fight depending on your choice if you really want to risk for a higher reward. That's the entire game until you come across the boss for the area. Now you have a lot of enemies in the later zones, environmental hazards, enemies that split into more enemies and a crammed area to fight with all this happening. Take too long and a special enemy is going to show up during your fight and two turns after it's spawn and you haven't cleaned up the current enemy mess because enemy reinforcement's also showed up, you are going to take serious damage if you're in their attack range, and it won't stop, they'll keep spawning. The characters that you play as don't seem to have any character development while you journey through the game. You get a little chat when you first come across them, but they don't say much after unless it's the boss enemy of that zone. To be honest, I would have hoped since there are areas in the game, each character would have some different starting area because of their bio's you can look up later just so they can have some identity. Some of them don't look like you would find them in a city.

I enjoyed this game a lot. Specifically, I found the game mechanics to be a bit odd, but they actually made more sense as the challenge grew near the end of a "campaign," and every other aspect of the game was fun and pretty engaging and challenging! Each of the characters seemed to possess unique bios, play styles, and visual designs (though they did not appear to have many unique lines of dialogue, oh well), and the music was pretty good. I believe that the most fun part of this game had to be the amount of challenge; I'm still blown away by how many variables can seemingly affect the challenge of the fights. Just, whatever you do, make sure you understand the conditions for success so that you don't accidentally get a premature game over for something really stupid. In summary, I really liked this game, and I will probably go back to it again some time. If you are looking for an interesting, fun new take on a deck-building strategy game that doesn't necessarily need a riveting story to propel it forward, then you should go ahead and give this game a try.
